subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub standardize Weekly/Monthly/All time popularity across publishers, skills, and plugins with shared temporal stats, publisher aggregation, and snapshot-pinned leaderboard pagination before shipping visible period tabs?
rationale: Current main has enough partial infrastructure to make narrow UI changes tempting, but the RFC’s cross-surface semantics, scoring, ownership attribution, and rollout/backfill choices require maintainer product intent.

options.title: Approve shared foundation first
options.body: Define scoring, attribution, low-activity behavior, and snapshot cursor semantics, then implement package, publisher, and leaderboard foundations before UI tabs.

options.title: Limit to existing trending
options.body: Keep the current skills/plugins Trending tabs and defer publisher/monthly alignment, accepting that browse surfaces will not share the same period contract.

options.title: Spec only for now
options.body: Document the desired period contract in specs and wait for a maintainer-sponsored implementation plan before changing code.

recommendation.title: Approve shared foundation first
recommendation.body: Define scoring, attribution, low-activity behavior, and snapshot cursor semantics, then implement package, publisher, and leaderboard foundations before UI tabs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest current-main routing candidate for browse and catalog contract decisions based on blame and merged PR metadata for the relevant paths.
